How is Idaho organized, and where do I start when I sell a house?

Idaho has 44 counties, and almost everything that touches a home sale runs through one of them. The county assessor values the property, the county treasurer bills and collects the tax, and the county recorder files the deed.

The counties differ enormously in size. Ada County is the most populous at 546,141 people, and Clark County is the smallest at 783, according to the Wikipedia county list built on Census Bureau estimates. By land area, Idaho County is the largest at 8,485 square miles and Payette County the smallest at 408.

Who handles property taxes on an Idaho house, and when are they due?

Idaho splits the work between two offices. The assessor sets value, and the treasurer bills and collects. Call the first about value and exemptions, and the second about balances, payoff figures and payment history.

Property is valued as of 12:01 a.m. on January 1 of the year the tax is levied (Idaho Code 63-205). Tax is due in full by December 20, or the owner can pay in two halves, with the second half due June 20 as long as the first was paid in full (Idaho Code 63-903). Unpaid tax carries interest of one percent per month under Idaho Code 63-1001.

  • An assessment appeal on the subsequent roll is due the fourth Monday of November, and the board of equalization can hear only timely appeals.
  • Filing an appeal does not pause payment of the tax.
  • If delinquent real property is not redeemed within three years, the tax collector must make a tax deed to the county.

You can still sell a house with tax due. The title or escrow company normally pays the balance from proceeds, so ask the treasurer for a written payoff with a good-through date before you list or accept an offer. Our Idaho property tax guide walks through appeals and relief programs, and the county pages for Ada County, Canyon County and Kootenai County list local offices.

What does the homestead exemption do when I sell?

Idaho uses the word homestead for two separate protections, and sellers often blur them. One lowers the tax on an owner-occupied home. The other shields part of the equity from creditors.

ProtectionStatuteAmount
Homeowner's tax exemptionIdaho Code 63-602GLesser of $125,000 or 50% of assessed market value
Judicial homesteadIdaho Code 55-1003Up to $175,000 of equity

The tax exemption belongs to the owner who lives in the house, so a buyer who plans to move in applies for a fresh one. The creditor protection also covers the proceeds of a good faith voluntary sale for one year if you intend to buy a new homestead, so keep that money identifiable. If you carry judgments or large unsecured debts, talk to an Idaho attorney before closing. Details are in our Idaho homestead exemption guide.

How does foreclosure work in Idaho, and how much time do I have?

Most Idaho home loans use a trust deed, and a trust deed can be foreclosed without a court case under Idaho Code 45-1506. The statute still builds in long notice periods.

  • Notice of sale must be mailed by registered or certified mail at least 120 days before the trustee's sale.
  • The notice must be published once a week for four successive weeks, with the last publication at least 30 days before the sale.
  • Anyone may bid at the sale, including the lender.
  • The buyer at the sale is entitled to possession on the tenth day after it.

The homeowner also has a window to catch up. Within 115 days of the recording of the notice of default, the owner can pay the amount due, plus costs and fees, and reinstate the loan. If a lender goes to court instead, the same section lets the owner cure at any time before a decree of foreclosure is entered.

If you have received a notice of default, the clock matters more than the price. Selling before the trustee's sale lets you pay the lender from proceeds and keep any equity. Call the lender or a housing counselor early, and confirm the sale date from the recorded notice at the county recorder.

What happens to an inherited house in Idaho?

Idaho has no inheritance tax, no gift tax, and its estate tax expired in 2004, according to the Idaho State Tax Commission. Federal estate tax applies only above $15,000,000 for deaths in 2026, so most heirs owe no death tax on the house itself.

The harder question is who can sign the deed. Idaho follows the Uniform Probate Code, and a court normally appoints a personal representative who can sell estate real property under Idaho Code 15-3-715. A small estate affidavit is limited to a probate estate of $100,000 and reaches personal property, not real estate. Probate generally must be started within three years of death, with exceptions.

Some practical points for heirs:

  • A transfer by a fiduciary or from a decedent's estate is exempt from the seller property condition disclosure form under Idaho Code 55-2505.
  • The homestead exemption continues for the year of death and the following tax year while the home stays in the estate.
  • Property tax keeps arriving while probate is open.

Our Idaho probate guide and estate and inheritance tax guide cover the steps in order. If a quitclaim deed is part of the plan, read the quitclaim deed guide first, because that deed passes only what the signer owns.

What should I know about tenants when I sell an Idaho rental?

A sale does not cancel a tenant's rights. If a rental changes hands during a tenancy, the new owner becomes liable to refund the security deposit under Idaho Code 6-321(3). Make sure the deposit amounts and lease dates in your records match what the tenant believes.

  • Deposits must be refunded within 21 days if the agreement sets no time, and always within 30 days after the tenant surrenders the premises.
  • For unpaid rent, a landlord serves a three day written notice demanding payment or possession (Idaho Code 6-303).
  • A month to month tenancy at will ends by written notice of not less than one month (Idaho Code 55-208).
  • After a court judgment, a residential tenant has 72 hours to remove belongings (Idaho Code 6-316).

If you want the house empty at closing, start the written notice early and keep a copy. Eviction is a court process with fixed steps, and the sheriff carries out removal. Our Idaho landlord tenant guide covers repair claims and notices in more detail.

What does a cash sale as-is mean in Idaho?

It means the buyer takes the house in its current condition, with no repair requests, and pays without waiting on a mortgage approval. A buyer may still inspect and ask questions.

Closing still goes through a title or escrow company, which confirms who holds title, pays off liens, and prorates current year tax. Ask that company how the tax will be handled, and who actually sends the payment to the treasurer. Counties warn about this timing. Kootenai County, for example, notes that escrow may not pay the treasurer if closing happens before the annual tax information is available.

Before we make an offer we review the property, the title and the county tax status. We do not quote a price without seeing the house, and you owe nothing if you turn the offer down. Idaho also taxes the gain on a sale. The state allows a 60 percent deduction for gain on Idaho real property held at least 12 months, and the Idaho income tax rate for 2025 is 5.3 percent. Our Idaho capital gains guide explains how that interacts with the federal home sale exclusion.

Where do Idaho sellers find local help in their own city?

Start with the page for your city and then the county office behind it. The Treasure Valley pages include Boise, Meridian and Nampa. North Idaho sellers can read about Coeur d'Alene and Post Falls. Eastern and southern Idaho are covered by pages such as Idaho Falls, Pocatello and Twin Falls.

If your property sits in a county we do not list, call that county's assessor, treasurer and recorder directly, since the county website is the final word on fees and forms.

Frequently asked questions

How many counties does Idaho have?

Idaho has 44 counties. Ada County is the most populous, and each county has its own assessor, treasurer and recorder.

When are Idaho property taxes due?

Tax is due in full by December 20, or in two halves with the second due June 20. Ask the county treasurer for a payoff before closing.

Is Idaho foreclosure judicial?

Most home loans use trust deeds, which can be foreclosed without a court case. Notice of sale must go out at least 120 days before the trustee's sale.

Can I sell a house with back taxes in Idaho?

Yes. The balance is normally paid from proceeds at closing, so get a written payoff from the treasurer first.

Does Idaho have an inheritance tax?

No. The Idaho State Tax Commission says Idaho has no inheritance or gift tax, and its estate tax expired in 2004.

Do I need probate to sell an inherited house?

Usually. The small estate affidavit reaches personal property up to $100,000, not real estate, so a personal representative typically signs the deed.

What happens to my tenant if I sell?

The tenant keeps their rights, and the new owner becomes liable for the security deposit. Written notice rules apply if you want the house vacant.

Do I have to make repairs before a cash sale?

No. A cash sale as-is means the buyer takes the house in its current condition.
